Section 1(b) permits, notwithstanding section 1(a)(i), purchases for value or sales made on or before 11:59 p.m. eastern standard time on November 11, 2021 solely to divest securities held as of 9:30 a.m. eastern standard time on January 11, 2021 in a company listed under section 4(a)(i). Executive Order 13974 of January 13, 2021 amended the clause, and Executive Order 14032 of June 3, 2021 then restated it as section 1(c)(i), which permits divestment purchases and sales by a United States person of securities of a person listed in the Annex "prior to" 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on June 3, 2022; the November 11, 2021 date in the original wording therefore never operated as the end of the window. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments the restatement is an amendment and the clause continues, as amended, so the first end is the end of the restated window, June 3, 2022, by the restated clause's own terms (the permission covers transactions before 12:01 a.m. on that date, so the last day of permission is June 2, 2022; recording the stated date June 3, 2022 inclusive follows the owner ruling on until-dates and the exclusive reading is the alternative). The held eCFR text of 31 CFR 586.201 shows the prohibition itself remains in force, so only this transitional divestment permission ended. If the restatement were instead treated as ending the original clause, the first end would be 2021-06-03, the date of Executive Order 14032; the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments does not support that reading. Before: the original section 1(b) window through November 11, 2021 for securities held on January 11, 2021 in a company listed under section 4(a)(i). After: the restated section 1(c)(i) window to June 3, 2022 for securities of Annex persons. The substance changed, so a reviewer should compare the restated section 1(c) in the held text of Executive Order 14032 with this clause.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13959 (November 12, 2020, 85 FR 73185) declares a national emergency over securities investments that finance certain companies of the People's Republic of China and prohibits United States persons from transacting in their securities. The order is operative on 2026-10-14 as amended. Executive Order 13974 of January 13, 2021 amended sections 1(b) and (c), 4(a)(ii) and (iii) and 4(e); Executive Order 14032 of June 3, 2021 replaced and superseded sections 1 through 5, as amended, in their entirety to read as restated, replaced the Annex, renumbered section 6 as section 7, and revoked Executive Order 13974 in its entirety. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments each restated clause continues, as amended; the amendments are later events on the clauses and the President's own notices describe the change as 14032 having amended Executive Order 13959 and revoked Executive Order 13974. The only clause that ended is section 1(b), the transitional divestment window, whose restated form ran out on June 3, 2022 by its own terms. The order depends on the national emergency it declared, which the held Presidential notices of November 9, 2021 (86 FR 62711), November 8, 2022 (87 FR 68017), November 3, 2023 (88 FR 76987), November 7, 2024 (89 FR 88869) and November 5, 2025 (90 FR 50739) continue year by year; the last continues it beyond November 12, 2025, to a date after the cutoff. The held eCFR text of 31 CFR 586.201 and 586.404, checked as of 2026-10-14, still implements the order as amended. Executive Order 14294 of May 9, 2025, a general policy order on criminal regulatory offenses, does not name this order and does not end any clause.

savings.reason: The order is not terminated, so no residual effect after an ending arises. The one ended clause, the section 1(b) divestment window, is a permission whose end leaves the section 1(a) prohibition in force and creates no surviving right. The order contains no savings clause that preserves a measure beyond a revocation; section 1(d) applies the prohibitions notwithstanding earlier contracts, licenses or permits. The bounded searches found no later instrument that revokes the order or preserves part of it.
